topic_summary: Analysis of competing constitutional interpretations regarding the ultimate locus of interpretive authority in state legal systems. The core contest: whether elected legislatures possess final sovereignty over law (parliamentary supremacy reading) or whether courts/fundamental rights operate as superior constraints on legislative action (judicial supremacy reading). This determines who legitimately adjudicates the boundary of permissible state coercion.

key_entities: Popular sovereignty (democratic mandate grounding legislative authority)
key_tensions: Democratic mandate (legislature as popular will) vs Rule of law (courts as rights guardians)
Written constitution as supreme law vs Legislature as ultimate interpreter of written constitution
mechanisms: Judicial review (courts strike down legislation as unconstitutional)
Legislative override (parliament reasserts authority via supermajority or notwithstanding clause)
Constitutional amendment process (who controls kernel revision)
absences: Executive branch role in interpretive contests (treated as derivative rather than independent interpreter)
Comparative empirical outcomes: do different readings produce measurably different coercion patterns or only different legitimation narratives

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The constitutional framework as a fixed reference point grounding legitimate interpretive authority over state coercion
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between legislative bodies (claiming democratic mandate) and judiciary (claiming constitutional fidelity or fundamental rights guardianship)

readings.commitment: Elected legislature possesses final interpretive authority; no judicial authority to void parliamentary acts
readings.authority_grounding: Democratic mandate via electoral accountability; legislative body as embodiment of popular sovereignty
readings.expected_structural_delta: Legislature enters beneficiary set for interpretive discretion; judiciary excluded from ultimate authority; coercion legitimated via electoral mandate rather than rights-grounding

readings.commitment: Courts possess final interpretive authority via constitutional/fundamental rights guardianship; legislative acts subject to judicial nullification
readings.authority_grounding: Constitutional text as supreme law OR unwritten fundamental rights as pre-political constraints; judicial expertise in rights interpretation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Judiciary enters beneficiary set for interpretive authority; legislature subordinated; coercion legitimated via rights-compliance rather than democratic will

readings.commitment: No single branch possesses final interpretive authority; constitution constructed through inter-branch dialogue and political contestation
readings.authority_grounding: Structural ambiguity in constitutional design; interpretive authority distributed across branches via checks and balances
readings.expected_structural_delta: Authority dispersed; interpretive contests resolved through political mechanisms (amendment, appointment, budget control) rather than singular adjudication; higher tolerance for interpretive instability

axiom_contradictions.basis: Cannot simultaneously hold that legislature possesses final interpretive authority (supremacy axiom) and that courts may nullify legislative acts as unconstitutional (judicial review axiom). One branch's finality requires the other's subordination.

axes.human_readable: Parliamentary Supremacy Reading (Legislature as Final Interpreter)
axes.structural_delta: Constitutional framework read as granting elected legislature ultimate interpretive authority; no external constraint on parliamentary lawmaking
axes.primary_observable: Presence/absence of constitutional judicial review; legislative override mechanisms; explicit constitutional supremacy clauses
axes.selection_reason: First reading selected: pure democratic accountability grounding; highest structural clarity; distinct epsilon from coordinate model

axes.human_readable: Judicial Supremacy Reading (Courts as Constitutional Guardians)
axes.structural_delta: Constitutional framework read as establishing courts as final arbiters of constitutional meaning via judicial review power
axes.primary_observable: Scope of judicial review; presence of constitutional courts; enforceability of judicial nullification of legislation
axes.selection_reason: Second reading selected: axiom-contradictory to parliamentary supremacy; rights-grounding versus mandate-grounding; same epsilon bin but opposite beneficiary structure

axes.structural_delta: Constitutional framework read as establishing no final interpreter; interpretive authority constructed through inter-branch contestation
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of inter-branch interpretive conflicts; use of non-judicial mechanisms (appointments, budgets, amendments) to resolve constitutional disputes
axes.selection_reason: Third reading selected: intermediate epsilon; neither pure supremacy claim; structurally distinct mechanism (political resolution vs legal adjudication); captures hybrid/ambiguity space

axes.human_readable: Popular Sovereignty Reading (Constitution as Revocable Delegation)
axes.structural_delta: Constitutional authority derives from ongoing popular consent; people retain extra-institutional interpretive authority via revolution/referendum
axes.primary_observable: Constitutional amendment difficulty; presence of popular referendum mechanisms; revolutionary legitimacy discourse
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream grounding for parliamentary supremacy but lower epsilon; indirect legitimation narrative rather than direct interpretive mechanism

axes.structural_delta: Constitutional authority limited by natural/fundamental rights existing prior to and independent of constitutional text
axes.primary_observable: Invocation of unenumerated rights; natural law reasoning in judicial opinions; rights discourse independence from positive law
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: specific grounding mechanism for judicial supremacy; captured within judicial_supremacy_reading authority structure; would produce near-duplicate constraint story

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Constitution as revocable delegation from popular sovereign
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream legitimation narrative for parliamentary supremacy; lower epsilon; indirect rather than operational interpretive mechanism

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Pre-political rights as superior constraint on positive law
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Specific grounding for judicial supremacy; captured within judicial_supremacy_reading authority structure; would produce structurally redundant constraint story

omegas.description: Do the three readings produce measurably different coercion patterns, or only different legitimation narratives for similar state behavior? If the latter, the kernel contest is performative rather than structural.
omegas.source: Absence Inventory (§1.1): Comparative empirical outcomes not addressed in research context

omegas.description: Executive branch role in interpretive contests systematically absent. Does executive possess independent interpretive authority (coordinate construction variant) or is it derivative of legislative/judicial positions?
omegas.source: Absence Inventory (§1.1): Executive treated as background rather than independent interpreter

omegas.description: Who controls the constitutional amendment process may be the true ultimate interpreter. If legislature controls amendment but courts control current interpretation, apparent judicial supremacy may be legislative supremacy deferred.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2: Mechanism for kernel revision itself determines reading stability

omegas.description: Empirical constitutional systems may exhibit reading drift: formal judicial supremacy systems where courts defer to legislatures (Canada notwithstanding clause underuse), or parliamentary supremacy systems with de facto judicial review (UK pre-HRA common law constitutionalism). Readings may be unstable under political pressure.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3: Beneficiary structure suggests readings are not equilibria but contested positions subject to drift

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel/reading decomposition appropriate: readings hold axiom-contradictory positions (parliamentary vs judicial finality), would emit structurally different constraints (different beneficiary/victim sets, different extractiveness mechanisms), and share a common substrate (constitutional framework as interpretive authority source). Coordinate construction reading offers intermediate position with distinct mechanism (political rather than legal resolution).
